_meta.description: Disease class -> treatment lookup for rice in the Nepal Terai. Structured data, not model output: the classifier decides WHAT the lesion is, this table decides what to DO about it. Nothing here is generated by an LLM.
sources: Nepal Agricultural Research Council (NARC) - Rice Research Programme, integrated pest management recommendations
IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank - rice disease management
Plant Quarantine and Pesticide Management Centre (PQPMC), Nepal - registered pesticide list
_meta.review_note: Chemical names and doses must be re-checked against the current PQPMC registered list before any real farmer sees them. Treat this file as reviewed reference data, not as final agronomic advice.

healthy.label: Healthy
cultural_practice: No action needed. Continue routine monitoring.
Re-photograph in 7 days, or sooner if you see new spots.
healthy.notes: A healthy classification is not a guarantee the field is disease-free - it only describes the leaf in this photo.

brown_spot.label: Brown Spot

chemical_treatment.timing: At first appearance; repeat after 12-15 days if lesions continue to spread

cultural_practice: Brown spot is strongly associated with potassium and silicon deficiency - check the fertilizer plan before spraying again.
Avoid prolonged water stress; the disease worsens in under-irrigated fields.
Use certified, treated seed next season.
brown_spot.notes: Recurring brown spot usually signals a soil nutrition problem rather than a fungicide problem. Spraying alone will not fix a potassium-deficient field.

leaf_blast.label: Rice Leaf Blast

chemical_treatment.timing: At first lesion appearance, and again at panicle initiation if pressure persists

cultural_practice: Stop or reduce nitrogen top-dressing - excess nitrogen makes blast substantially worse.
Maintain a thin standing water layer; alternate wetting and drying raises blast risk.
Blast spreads fastest in cool nights with long leaf wetness - inspect daily during such weather.
leaf_blast.notes: Leaf blast can progress to neck blast at flowering, which is far more damaging to yield. Early action matters more than for any other disease in this list.

hispa.label: Rice Hispa
hispa.pathogen: Dicladispa armigera (insect pest, not a fungus)

chemical_treatment.application: Foliar spray targeting the leaf whorl
chemical_treatment.timing: When more than 1 adult per hill or heavy leaf scraping is visible

cultural_practice: Clip and destroy heavily damaged leaf tips before spraying - this removes most of the eggs and grubs.
Hand-collect adults early morning when they are sluggish; effective on small plots.
Avoid excess nitrogen, which encourages the lush growth hispa prefers.
hispa.notes: This is an insect, so a fungicide will do nothing. Getting the class right matters more here than the dose.

below_gate.message: The image was not clear enough for a confident diagnosis, so no treatment is being recommended.
below_gate.message_ne: तस्बिर स्पष्ट नभएकोले निश्चित निदान गर्न सकिएन, त्यसैले कुनै उपचार सिफारिस गरिएको छैन।
actions: Take another photo in daylight, filling the frame with a single affected leaf.
Hold the phone steady about 15-20 cm from the leaf; avoid shadows and background clutter.
If the next photo is also inconclusive, contact your local agriculture extension officer (Krishi Gyan Kendra, Siraha).
